core.title: Route each acceptance to a layer plane by its keyword cues
core.given: An acceptance criterion is being assigned or reassigned to a layer plane
core.when: The plane is chosen for that acceptance
core.then: Choose the layer plane, from the stack's layer roles, that the acceptance's keyword cues indicate in the plane keyword table.
prefer: presentation cues: display, visible, screen, render, animation, button, form, modal.
application cues: workflow, orchestrate, use case, policy, state, saga.
domain cues: rule, validate, aggregate, entity, invariant, business.
integration cues: database, persist, external, queue, api, webhook, repository.
avoid: Assigning a plane that contradicts the acceptance's keyword cues (e.g. putting a 'persist' or 'webhook' acceptance in the presentation plane).
Rewording an acceptance just to hit or avoid a keyword so that a preferred plane gets selected.
core.why: The keyword-derived plane drives the downstream plane-to-layer-sequence routing. A wrong plane sends the work to the wrong layers.
evidence: Each acceptance's assigned plane matches the plane whose keywords appear in its text.
The plane that the downstream layer-sequence selection uses equals the keyword-derived plane.
verification: The check consults this rule's plane keyword table (layer plane -> routing cue terms) and is a plain term match against the acceptance's text; the cue table is rule data (see prefer), not profile data.

Cue terms decide the plane but are not the rule's only trigger: assignment or reassignment of a plane to a new or existing acceptance also fires it, and detecting that needs a diff-level or routing-step observer (needs_new_observer).
Scope: the rule applies in any phase and in any artifact or container where an acceptance is routed; particular plan artifacts are examples, not required gates.
Not covered by the term match: whether an acceptance was reworded to hit or avoid a cue (the gaming guard in avoid) stays an agent-facing judgment, not something the cue match verifies.

fires: A new acceptance criterion is assigned a layer plane.
An existing acceptance is reassigned to a plane, or its plane is re-derived, outside any authoring or revision step (e.g. during routing or re-triage).
An acceptance's wording now has cues for a different plane than the one assigned.
A plane assignment is needed to select the layer sequence for the work (the downstream sequence-selection convention).
doesNotFire: Implementing code for an acceptance whose plane is already assigned and is not being changed.
Editing prose or docs that contain no acceptance criteria.
Reviewing test code where no acceptance plane assignment is involved.

profileRequirements.meaning: The layer roles that are the candidate planes: the plane keyword table routes each acceptance to one of these roles, and the core's cue lists key the standard layer roles (presentation, application, domain, integration).

bunOnly.text: Term plane_keywords ('Plane keywords'): layer -> routing keywords.
bunOnly.reason: Names the ATDD-Bun sidecar's term-registry entry (term id and label), a realization detail of this rule. The core describes the keyword table generically in its verification array; the table's neutral content is carried by prefer[0..3].

bunOnly.text: Plans, wagons and WMBTs are examples, not required gates.
bunOnly.reason: 'wagon' and 'WMBT' are ATDD-Bun artifact kinds (layout/urn profile concepts). The core states the scope generically - any artifact or container where an acceptance is routed, with plan artifacts as examples, not gates - in its verification array.

neutralityNotes: The rule is almost entirely stack-neutral: it operates on acceptance text and layer-plane roles, not on files or tooling. The cue vocabulary and the four standard plane roles (presentation, application, domain, integration) are kept as core rule data, following the vocabulary's notProfileKeys guidance that rule-specific task terms live in core activation or the realization; a stack whose layer roles differ supplies its plane set through roles.layers and binds the cue-table keys to those roles. bun.json's fires reference the sibling rule id planner.criteria.sequence-routing; the core says 'the downstream layer-sequence selection (convention)' and each stack binds that to its own sequence-routing rule - the id itself has no numbered item slot and is noted here rather than in bunOnly. The 'wagon'/'WMBT' example naming in activation.facts[0]'s note and the sidecar term-registry entry 'plane_keywords' are ATDD-Bun realization details, recorded in bunOnly. The plain cue terms (e.g. api, webhook, database) are method vocabulary, not stack names, so they remain in the core. bun.json declares no severity or disposition, so the core's verification adds none.
